title: NRL Average Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay Using 38 Hours a Week
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the standard 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes NRL average salary context, tax, super, and fortnightly pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the standard way to compare them is to calculate the annual gross pay. The formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For most full-time roles, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you a consistent annual figure before tax, super, and other deductions.

For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00:
- Weekly pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly pay: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual gross: $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

This calculation assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### The NRL Average Salary as a Benchmark

You may have heard the **NRL average salary** mentioned in the news. That figure is an average for professional rugby league players, not a median for your job or industry. The NRL average salary includes base pay, match fees, and sometimes third-party agreements. It is calculated by the league or the players' association and can vary year to year. When you see that number, remember it is an average for a specific group of elite athletes, not a guide for your own hourly rate. For most workers, the relevant comparison is the award rate for your occupation or the National Minimum Wage.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour**, which equals $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum rate, making it **$33.05 per hour**. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. Many industries have specific award rates that may be higher than the minimum. You can check your award using [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual worker, your hourly rate should already include the 25% loading? No – the loading is added on top of the base rate. When using our [timesheet](/), you type your base hourly rate and check the box to add 25% casual loading. Never type a rate that already includes the loading. The system will calculate the loaded rate for you.

Superannuation guarantee is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your base pay. For example, if your base hourly rate is $30.00, your employer contributes an extra $3.60 per hour into your super fund. This contribution stops once your earnings reach the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). Super is not deducted from your take-home pay; it is an additional benefit.

### Tax on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of generally 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). This is an estimate only. It does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the $30.00 per hour example, your fortnightly gross is $2,280.00. After tax and Medicare, your take-home will be lower. You can use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see the net amount.

### What About the NRL Average Salary?

To reiterate, the **NRL average salary** is a headline figure for professional rugby league players. It is not a median for your job. If you are comparing your pay to that number, remember that it includes many components not present in a standard hourly wage. Your own pay should be evaluated against the award or minimum wage for your industry. The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings, which for full-time adult ordinary time was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026. That is a broader average across all industries. For more context, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Summary

To convert your hourly rate to annual pay:
1. Multiply your hourly rate by your weekly hours (assume 38 if full-time).
2. Multiply by 52 weeks.
3. Add 12% super on top (up to the contribution base).
4. Estimate tax using the resident rates above.

Remember, this is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For a personalised calculation, use [the timesheet](/).
